hot-desert-systems-landscapes-coastal-sy.d: Hot Desert Systems & Landscapes / Coastal Systems & Landscapes / Glacial Systems & Landscapes
terms: Antarctic Mass Loss
Net ice loss accelerating; West Antarctic ice sheet potentially destabilising; 3.3mm/year global sea level contribution.
Mass Balance
Annual accumulation minus ablation; positive balance = advance, negative = retreat; equilibrium line altitude divides.
Periglacial Processes
Frost shattering, solifluction, patterned ground; create stone circles, blockfields; common in tundra outside ice sheets.
Roches Moutonnees
Asymmetric bedrock landform: smooth abraded stoss slope, plucked lee side; indicates ice flow direction.
Subglacial Bedform
Streamlined hill formed beneath ice: drumlins, fluted moraines; debate over deformation till hypothesis (Boulton).
Warm vs Cold-Based Glaciers
Warm-based (Alpine) slide on meltwater film, erode actively; cold-based (Antarctic) frozen to bed, minimal erosion.
Boserup vs Malthus
Boserup: necessity drives technological innovation; Malthus: geometric population, arithmetic food, leading to crisis.
Carrying Capacity
Maximum population an environment can sustain; varies with technology and consumption; Malthusian limit debated.
Demographic Transition Model
Five stages of birth/death rate change; UK at Stage 4, Niger Stage 2, Japan Stage 5 (post-transition).
Ecological Footprint
Global hectares needed per capita; world average 2.7, USA 8.1, India 1.2; humanity consumes 1.75 Earths.
Replacement Fertility
Total fertility rate of 2.1 needed to maintain population; below this means demographic decline; many HICs at 1.5.
Zoonoses
Diseases transmitted from animals to humans; 70% of new pandemics; Ebola, COVID-19 linked to wildlife encroachment.
Circular Economy
Reduce-reuse-recycle replacing linear take-make-dispose; design for disassembly; Ellen MacArthur Foundation.
Critical Raw Materials
EU list of 30 materials essential to economy and supply-risky; includes rare earths, lithium, cobalt for green tech.
Lithium Triangle
Chile-Bolivia-Argentina contain 60% of world lithium reserves in salt flats; critical for EV batteries.
Peak Oil
Hubbert's 1956 theory of maximum extraction point; conventional peak debated; unconventional sources (shale) postponed.
Resource Curse
Paradox of resource-rich countries underperforming: Dutch Disease, corruption, conflict; e.g. DRC coltan, Niger oil.
Resource Frontier
Newly exploited regions: Arctic oil/gas, deep-sea mining; environmental risks balance against economic potential.

terms: Cycle Superhighways
London's segregated cycle lanes 2008-; reduce congestion; CS3 Cycleway carries 5,000+ cyclists/peak hour.
Eco-cities
Cities prioritising sustainability: Masdar City (UAE) zero-carbon; BedZED London first net-zero UK development.
Mumbai Dharavi
Asia's largest slum with 700,000-1 million people in 2 km2; thriving informal economy ($1 billion annual turnover).
Smart Cities
Use sensors, data and ICT to optimise services; Songdo, Korea; Curitiba's BRT; raises surveillance concerns.
Sustainable Urban Drainage
SUDS: permeable surfaces, swales, retention ponds mimic natural drainage; reduce urban flooding and pollution.
Urban Heat Island
Cities 1-3 degrees C warmer than rural surroundings; concrete absorbs heat, vehicles emit; London Heathrow most extreme.

Just Transition

Sustainable Development Goals

Vauban Freiburg
German eco-district built 1996-2006; car-light, passive houses, solar PV; model sustainable community.

Gender Inequality Index
Introduced UNDP HDR 2010; combines reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation.
Gini coefficient
Corrado Gini 1912; measures income inequality from 0 (equal) to 1 (one earner); South Africa 0.63 highest among major economies.
Human Development Index
Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen designed for UNDP 1990; combines life expectancy, education and GNI per capita PPP.
Multidimensional Poverty Index
OPHI / UNDP since 2010; tracks health, education and living standards; 1.1 billion poor in 2023.
Sustainable Development Goals
UN 2030 Agenda adopted September 2015; 17 goals and 169 targets, replacing the Millennium Development Goals 2000-15.
Air mass
A large body of air with broadly uniform temperature and humidity, classified by its source region, such as tropical maritime or polar continental.
Anticyclone
A high-pressure system with descending, diverging air giving settled, dry conditions — hot and sunny in summer, frosty or foggy in winter.
Depression
A mid-latitude low-pressure system formed where warm and cold air masses meet, bringing fronts, cloud, rainfall and strong winds.
Fronts
Boundaries between air masses; at a warm front warm air rises gently over cold air, while a cold front undercuts steeply, giving heavier showers.
Global atmospheric circulation
The Hadley, Ferrel and Polar cells redistribute heat from the equator towards the poles, creating belts of high and low pressure.
Global heat budget
The balance between incoming shortwave solar radiation and outgoing longwave radiation; a surplus at low latitudes and deficit at the poles drives circulation.

Loss of symbiotic algae when temperatures rise 1-2 degrees C above normal; Great Barrier Reef lost 50% of corals since 1995.
Gyres and Garbage Patches
Great Pacific Garbage Patch in North Pacific Gyre; 80,000 tonnes plastic, twice size of Texas.
Marine Protected Areas
UN target 30 by 30 protect 30% of oceans by 2030; current 8%; Chagos MPA 640,000km2 one of largest.
Ocean Acidification
pH dropped 0.1 since pre-industrial; threatens shell-forming organisms; oysters, pteropods, coral skeletons.
Overfishing
FAO: 35% of stocks fished beyond biological sustainability; cod collapse off Newfoundland 1992 still unrecovered.
Thermohaline Circulation
Global ocean conveyor driven by temperature and salinity; AMOC weakening 15% since 1950s due to Arctic melt.

global-development-connections-health-hu.d: Global Development & Connections (Health, Human Rights / Migration, Identity)
terms: Geopolitical intervention
Actions by states and organisations — development aid, sanctions or military action — intended to improve human rights or development, with contested outcomes.
Human rights
Universal entitlements set out in the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights, protected very unevenly across the world by laws and institutions.
Measuring development
Development can be measured economically using GDP per capita, or more broadly with the Human Development Index combining income, life expectancy and education.
National identity
A shared sense of belonging shaped by history, language and culture, which migration and globalisation can both enrich and contest.
National sovereignty
A state's authority to govern its own territory, increasingly challenged by globalisation, supranational institutions and international migration.
Types of migrant
Economic migrants move voluntarily for work, while refugees flee across borders from persecution or conflict; the two have different legal protections.

Benioff Zone
Inclined plane of seismicity below subducting plate; earthquakes deepen with distance from trench; defines subduction angle.
Hotspot Volcanism
Mantle plume independent of plate margins; Hawaii chain shows track as Pacific plate moves NW over Hawaiian plume.
Park's Disaster Response Curve
Stages: relief (hours-days), rehabilitation (weeks-months), reconstruction (years); LIC curves drop deeper than HIC.
Plate Tectonics Theory
1960s synthesis by Hess (seafloor spreading) and Wilson; lithospheric plates move on asthenosphere driven by mantle convection.
Pressure Release Theory
Bonin's mechanism: melting in subducting slabs caused by dehydration and lowered melting point under pressure.
Tohoku 2011
9.0 magnitude megathrust earthquake; 15m tsunami killed 18,500; Fukushima Daiichi nuclear meltdown; cost $235 billion.
Dynamic Equilibrium
State where inputs and outputs of energy/sediment are balanced; coast adjusts when conditions change.
Eustatic vs Isostatic
Eustatic = global sea level change (melting ice); isostatic = local land movement (post-glacial rebound in Scotland).
Holderness Cliffs
Yorkshire boulder clay coast; 1.8m/year erosion; fastest in Europe; Mappleton lost 4m/year before defences.
Maldives Sea Level Threat
1190 islands averaging 1.5m elevation; could be uninhabitable by 2050 with sea level rise; demonstrates LIC vulnerability.
Sediment Cell
Self-contained section of coast with sources, transport pathways and sinks; England has 11; e.g. cell 1 Berwick-Flamborough.
Shoreline Management Plans
DEFRA strategies: hold the line, advance, managed realignment, no active intervention; balance cost and benefit.
Cornwall Eden Project
Tim Smit's biome attraction in former clay pit (2001); 1 million annual visitors; symbol of regenerated post-industrial Cornwall.
Deindustrialisation
Decline of manufacturing share; UK manufacturing dropped from 35% of GDP (1970) to 10% (2020); Rust Belt and Northern UK.
Detroit Decline
Population fell from 1.85m (1950) to 640,000 (2020); car industry collapse, suburbanisation, racial tensions, 2013 bankruptcy.
Enterprise Zones
Government areas with tax reliefs and simplified planning; Tees Valley EZ aims to attract green tech investment.
Liverpool Capital of Culture 2008
European City of Culture spurred 6.5 billion regeneration around Albert Dock and Liverpool One; 9.7m visitor uplift.
Olympic Legacy
London 2012 regenerated Stratford with athletes' village (East Village), Westfield, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park.

Energy Mix
Combination of fuels in supply; UK 2023: gas 40%, renewables 25%, nuclear 15%, others; varies by country.
Energy Pathways
Routes from source to user; can be diversified for security; LNG terminals reduce pipeline dependence.
Hinkley Point C
UK new nuclear at £33 billion; 3.2 GW capacity; EDF and CGN financing; security and decarbonisation tensions.
OPEC+
Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (1960) plus Russia from 2016; controls 50% of world oil; cartel sets production.
Russia-Europe Gas
Pre-2022 Russia supplied 40% of EU gas; Nord Stream pipelines; invasion of Ukraine triggered diversification.
Strategic Petroleum Reserve
US emergency oil stockpile created after 1973 oil shock; 700 million barrels capacity; released to ease prices.
Drainage basin system
An open system where precipitation inputs are stored and transferred by interception, infiltration and throughflow, and leave as evapotranspiration and channel flow.
Human disruption of the cycle
Over-abstraction, deforestation and land-use change disrupt stores and flows, lowering water tables and intensifying drought and flood risk.
Storm hydrograph
A graph of river discharge following rainfall; flashy hydrographs have short lag times and high peaks, shaped by basin characteristics and human activity.
Water budget
The annual balance between precipitation, evapotranspiration and changes in storage, determining periods of soil moisture surplus, deficit and recharge.
Water insecurity
When safe, affordable water is insufficient, caused by physical scarcity of supply or economic scarcity from inadequate access and infrastructure.
Water management
Hard engineering such as dams, transfer schemes and desalination, and sustainable approaches like recycling and rainwater harvesting, attempt to close supply-demand gaps.
Endogenous Factors
Internal characteristics shaping place: location, topography, demographics, land use, history; root identity.
Exogenous Factors
External relationships: migration, capital flows, government policy, tourism; constantly reshape places.
Gentrification
Ruth Glass's 1964 term for middle-class arrival in working-class areas; rising rents displace original residents; e.g. Hackney.
Placelessness
Edward Relph's 1976 term for homogenised landscapes lacking distinctive character; e.g. airport terminals, chain stores.
Rebranding
Place marketing changing image to attract investment, residents, tourists; e.g. Liverpool Capital of Culture 2008.
Sense of Place
Subjective meanings attached to location: insider/outsider, near/far perceptions; studied by humanistic geographers like Tuan.

climate-change-disease-dilemmas-explorin.d: Climate Change / Disease Dilemmas / Exploring Oceans / Future of Food / Hazardous Earth
terms: Climate Justice
Recognition that LICs face greatest impacts but bear least responsibility; loss and damage fund agreed COP27 2022.
ENSO
El Nino Southern Oscillation; El Nino weakens trade winds, warms eastern Pacific; affects global weather patterns.
IPCC AR6 2021-23
Sixth Assessment Report: 'unequivocal' human warming; 1.5 degree breach likely before 2040; methane spike.
Net Zero
Balancing emissions and removals; UK 2008 Climate Change Act amended 2019 to 2050 target; requires rapid decarbonisation.
Radiative Forcing
Net change in energy balance at top of atmosphere; CO2 forcing 2.16 W/m2 above pre-industrial.
Tipping Points
Lenton's 2008 climate thresholds: Arctic ice, Amazon dieback, AMOC collapse, permafrost; abrupt nonlinear changes possible.

earths-life-support-systems-water-carbon.d: Earth's Life Support Systems (Water & Carbon Cycles)
terms: Carbon Sinks
Reservoirs storing more carbon than released: oceans (38,000 GtC), fossil fuels, terrestrial vegetation, soils.
Drainage Basin Hydrological Cycle
Open system: inputs (precipitation), outputs (evapotranspiration, discharge), stores (groundwater, vegetation).
Keeling Curve
Charles Keeling's continuous CO2 measurement from Mauna Loa since 1958; rose from 315 to 420+ ppm.
Ocean Acidification
pH dropped 0.1 since pre-industrial as oceans absorb 30% of anthropogenic CO2; threatens coral reefs and shellfish.
Permafrost Methane
Arctic permafrost contains 1,500 GtC; thawing releases methane (28x more potent than CO2) creating feedback loop.
Tropical Rainforest Hydrology
High evapotranspiration generates 50% of regional rainfall; deforestation reduces moisture recycling, prolongs droughts.
Climate change evidence
Ice cores, instrumental records and IPCC assessments link rising greenhouse gas concentrations to global warming, though responses remain politically contested.
Disease diffusion
Diseases spread by expansion, relocation and hierarchical diffusion; mapping outbreaks, as John Snow did for cholera, guides intervention.
Food security
Exists when all people at all times have access to sufficient, safe, nutritious food; it is threatened by population growth, climate change and conflict.
Mitigation vs adaptation
Mitigation tackles causes, such as cutting greenhouse gas emissions, while adaptation adjusts to impacts, such as flood defences and drought-resistant crops.
Ocean systems
Oceans regulate climate by storing heat and carbon; key threats include warming, acidification, overfishing and plastic pollution.
Tectonic hazards
Earthquakes and volcanic eruptions concentrate at plate boundaries; the risk they pose depends on magnitude, exposure, vulnerability and resilience.
